If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecasts to smooth volatility.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast diverges >1.5% from recent history, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward correction to late horizon (16–30 days) to align with mean reversion.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 10% of recent low, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon to capture rebound potential.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is above 10% of recent high, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon to avoid overcorrection.
